Directions: Use the information about beavers and your knowledge of science to answer each question that follows.
Title: Beavers
Content: Beavers are mammals that are found in most of North America. Beavers have several body structures that help them live.

:ibox:• A large, flat tail helps the beaver stand upright on land and steer when swimming. The beaver also slaps the water with its tail to warn when danger is near.
• Thick fur keeps the beaver warm and protects it in the water.
• Webbed back feet make it easier for the beaver to swim.
The beaver also has long front teeth that grow throughout its life. The front teeth have a sharp edge. A beaver's teeth are shown in Picture `2`.
The beaver uses its sharp teeth to cut down trees.

:ibox:• The beaver eats the inner bark of the trees.
• The beaver uses the trees to build a lodge, in which it lives.
The beaver also uses the trees to make a dam across a stream, which changes the environment, as shown in Picture `3`.

:ibox:• The dam slows the water flow to form a pond.
• Wooded areas or meadows are changed into wetlands.
• Some plants die when the area floods.
• Other plants are able to grow better because of the water.
• The pond forms a home for water plants and animals.
• Dead trees give homes to insects and birds.
